name: Labor-representation certification shock
mechanism: A newly public NLRB election outcome or certification changes the observable labor-representation state of an employer. The economic channel is potential labor-cost, bargaining-power and operational-governance change; no return sign is assumed ex ante.
event_clock: Earliest reproducible NLRB public result/certification boundary. Current public result pages expose Tally Issued Date and the NLRB states that election reports count elections in the month the outcome is certified. If no time-of-day can be proven, use the next regular trading-session boundary rather than inferring an intraday clock.
cheap_falsifiers: shift the public-result boundary by one to five trading sessions
permute employer-to-issuer mappings within the frozen event universe
randomize outcome labels while preserving election counts and calendar structure
inject later case updates/certifications and verify the historical prefix is unchanged
gates: public-observation clock or conservative next-session rule
source_basis: DiNardo et al., Long-Run Impacts of Unions on Firms: New Evidence from Financial Markets (NBER Working Paper 14709; QJE 2012)
notes: Discovery lead only. This file does not establish PIT validity or performance authorization.
Current NLRB public search results expose more than 35,000 election records and historical pagination, but historical completeness, immutable reconstruction and issuer mapping remain unproven.
